St. Zosimas of Palestine

St. Zosimas of Palestine · St. Zosima of Palestine · St. Abba Zosimas · Zosimas

Period
Received chronology places his death around 560
Region
Palestine; Jordan wilderness
Titles / vocation
Monastic · Priest
Commemoration
April 4

Introduction

St. Zosimas is the Palestinian monk and priest remembered for meeting St. Mary of Egypt, bringing her Communion and burying her.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundMeeting St. Mary of EgyptDeathCommemoration and identityChronology
Death / martyrdom

Peaceful death around 560 in the received life

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA identifies St. Zosimas as a monk in Palestine. The longer life of St. Mary of Egypt describes his move from a monastery near Caesarea to one by the Jordan after he becomes troubled by the thought that he has already attained spiritual maturity.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening identification · [undefined] Source reading · Opening account of St. Zosimas and his change of monastery

Meeting St. Mary of Egypt

Following the monastery’s Lenten custom, he enters the wilderness and encounters St. Mary of Egypt. She tells him about her earlier life and repentance. As a priest he later brings her Holy Communion. When he returns again, he finds her dead and buries her. These events belong to the received life rather than a newly reconstructed eyewitness biography.

[undefined] Source reading · Desert encounter, request for Communion and burial narrative

Death

The OCA’s short entry says that St. Zosimas lived to a great age and died around 560. It does not give a martyrdom or execution account. Its received chronology should not be pressed into an exact modern birth date.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Final sentence

Commemoration and identity

His commemoration is April 4. His identity is the Palestinian priest in St. Mary’s story, distinct from other monastics named St. Zosimas, including Russian Saints of later centuries.

[1] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Title, commemoration heading and identification
